title: The augmented open tensor square after normalized total limit
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each small pro-etale site put $B_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and use the ordinary unbounded module derived category $D(B_W)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Open extension and restriction mean exact ringed-slice functors $e_!\dashv e^*$, applied termwise [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact].
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-open-immersion], $K\in D^b_c(U,R)$ and $P\in D^b_c(X,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. For $H\in D(B_W)$ write $H_n=H\otimes^L_{B_W}(A_n)_W$ and $Q_W(H)_\bullet=(\operatorname{Res}_n H_n)_n$, with the strict quotient transitions; $\operatorname{Res}_n$ forgets to $B_W$-modules along $B_W\to(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Use flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], the total right derived inverse limit on strict towers, and its normalized Roos model and augmentation comparison [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit].
Put $H=j_!K\otimes^L_{B_X}P$ and $H_U=K\otimes^L_{B_U}j^*P$, with section-normalized open tensor isomorphism $\gamma^B:H\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!H_U$ [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. On the flat-term K-flat quotient representatives let
$$T_n=\operatorname{Res}_n((j_!K)_n\otimes^L_{(A_n)_X}P_n),\qquad S_n=\operatorname{Res}_n(K_n\otimes^L_{(A_n)_U}j^*P_n).$$
Use the simultaneous strict quotient transitions, augmentations $c_T:\Delta H\to T_\bullet$, $c_S:\Delta H_U\to S_\bullet$, and strict open tensor isomorphism $\gamma_\bullet:T_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}JS_\bullet$ of [lem-sf-open-tensor-quotient-augmentation]. Here $J$ is termwise ringed open extension after scalar restriction. Let $a_T:H\to L_XT_\bullet$ and $a_S:H_U\to L_US_\bullet$ be the actual derived maps of those augmentations, where $L_W=R\lim$. Let $\lambda_S:j_!L_US_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}L_XJS_\bullet$ be the signed, augmentation-normalized comparison of [lem-sf-open-roos-extension-comparison].
Under the defining completed tensor identifications [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], the maps $a_T,a_S$ are respectively the actual quotient tensor-completion maps $\chi_{j_!K,P}$ and $\chi_{K,j^*P}$ [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion, def-sf-tensor-completion-comparison]. Both maps are isomorphisms, and the following is an equality of actual morphisms in $D(B_X)$:
$$L_X(\gamma_\bullet)\circ a_T=\lambda_S\circ j_!(a_S)\circ\gamma^B.$$
The equality uses the specified augmentations, whose first coordinates are their quotient maps and whose shifted coordinates are zero, with every quotient transition retained. No finite-Tor hypothesis over $A_n$ is imposed.

proof.text: By [lem-sf-open-roos-extension-comparison], $U,X$ are qcqs and $\ell$ is invertible on both. By [lem-sf-open-tensor-quotient-augmentation], $j_!K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ and $j^*P\in D^b_c(U,R)$. Thus the pairs $(j_!K,P)$ on $X$ and $(K,j^*P)$ on $U$ satisfy all hypotheses of the constructible tensor-completion theorem.

source.place: Lemmas 6.5.5 and 6.5.8(2),(3), pp.49–50; explicit actual quotient-unit normalization in the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: Apply [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion] to those two pairs. Its actual map is the quotient augmentation into the derived limit of the finite tensor tower. The defining completed tensors in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] are precisely $L_XT_\bullet$ and $L_US_\bullet$. The first-coordinate quotient maps and zero shifted coordinates agree with the normalized presentation of [def-sf-tensor-completion-comparison]. Therefore $a_T=\chi_{j_!K,P}$ and $a_S=\chi_{K,j^*P}$ under those defining identifications, and both are isomorphisms.

source.place: Lemmas 6.5.5 and 6.5.8(2),(3), pp.49–50; explicit actual quotient-unit normalization in the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: The strict equality from [lem-sf-open-tensor-quotient-augmentation] is $\gamma_\bullet c_T=J(c_S)\Delta(\gamma^B)$. In the natural normalized signed Roos model of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit], the chain map induced by $\gamma_\bullet$ is $\prod_n\gamma_n$ on each summand. Consequently the two augmented maps into that model have respective coordinates $((\gamma_nc_{T,n})_n,0)$ and $((J(c_{S,n})\gamma^B)_n,0)$, equal by the strict equality. Localizing this equality and using the natural Roos identifications gives $L_X(\gamma_\bullet)a_T=a_{Jc_S}\gamma^B$. Strict commutation with every transition ensures that these are chain maps for $d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$, with the specified signs.

proof.text: Apply the augmentation clause of [lem-sf-open-roos-extension-comparison] to $D=H_U$, $M_\bullet=S_\bullet$ and $c=c_S$. It gives $a_{Jc_S}=\lambda_Sj_!(a_S)$, for the specified product comparison on both signed summands. Substitution in step 3 yields $L_X(\gamma_\bullet)a_T=\lambda_Sj_!(a_S)\gamma^B$. Together with step 2 this proves every assertion. The argument uses the simultaneous strict augmentations, so it retains the quotient transitions and the zero shifted coordinates; none of its cited hypotheses requires finite Tor-amplitude over $A_n$.
